title: Physics
tagline: Why falling objects, light, atoms, and the expanding universe follow related rules.
description: Follow the experiments and arguments behind motion, heat, light, relativity, and quantum physics. Worked examples unpack the equations; short questions let you test the ideas before exploring what remains unresolved.
researchIntro: Recent papers, reports, and announcements, with an explanation of the result, its relevance, and the limits described in the source.

title: Chemistry
tagline: How atoms join, reactions unfold, and new substances acquire useful properties.
description: Start with atoms and bonds, then follow reactions through energy, speed, and equilibrium. Use that foundation to understand medicines, materials, living chemistry, and the instruments that identify an unknown sample.
researchIntro: Recent papers, reports, and announcements, with an explanation of the result, its relevance, and the limits described in the source.

title: Economics
tagline: How choices, incentives, and institutions shape the economy people live in.
description: Work through prices, market failures, jobs, growth, money, trade, and finance. Numerical examples make the models concrete; historical cases and research show where they help, where they fail, and who gains or loses.
researchIntro: Recent papers, reports, and announcements, with an explanation of the result, its relevance, and the limits described in the source.

title: Mathematics
tagline: Understand the patterns, work the calculations, and see why the methods hold.
description: Build from arithmetic and algebra to calculus, probability, statistics, and linear algebra. Follow worked calculations, try a question yourself, and use the formula sheet when you need a method again. The history explains what problems led people to invent these tools.
researchIntro: Recent papers, reports, and announcements, with an explanation of the result, its relevance, and the limits described in the source.

title: Artificial Intelligence
tagline: How models learn patterns, generate answers, and fail in revealing ways.
description: Start with a fitted line and build toward neural networks, image generators, and language models. Learn how training works, how to judge a result, and how data and design choices shape behavior. Practical examples connect the mechanisms with their uses and limits.
researchIntro: Recent papers, reports, and announcements, with an explanation of the result, its relevance, and the limits described in the source.

title: History
tagline: What happened, how we know, and how people understood their own choices.
description: Three connected routes through the past: the ancient world, Europe, and East Asia. Follow events in sequence, compare the sources behind them, and examine competing explanations. Timelines and reference entries help you return to the dates and people you need.
researchIntro: Recent papers, reports, and announcements, with an explanation of the result, its relevance, and the limits described in the source.

title: Biology
tagline: How living systems turn molecules into cells, bodies, and ecosystems.
description: Follow energy and information through cells, genes, evolution, organs, and ecosystems. Mechanisms and scale estimates explain how the parts work together; experiments show how biologists know, and biotechnology tests what they can change.
researchIntro: Recent papers, reports, and announcements, with an explanation of the result, its relevance, and the limits described in the source.

title: Computer Science
tagline: The ideas behind working software: computation, information, and reliable systems.
description: Trace a page request from bits and logic to networks, databases, and security. Along the way, learn what algorithms can do, what makes them efficient, and why systems fail. Small examples connect the theory with decisions programmers and users encounter.
researchIntro: Recent papers, reports, and announcements, with an explanation of the result, its relevance, and the limits described in the source.

title: Psychology and Cognitive Science
tagline: How minds learn, brains work, and experience becomes a scientific question.
description: Follow experiments from perception and memory to emotion, development, and social behavior. Learn how neurons and brain networks support these abilities, then examine sleep, consciousness theories, brain decoding, and the limits of the evidence.
researchIntro: Studies of cognition, neuroscience, and consciousness. Each entry distinguishes the measured result from its interpretation, including the participants, methods, and limits on generalization.

title: Engineering and How Things Work
tagline: Trace forces, energy, and information through the things people build.
description: Use kettles, bridges, gears, pipes, circuits, and robots to understand design. Worked calculations connect physical laws with materials, manufacturing, control, reliability, and the trade-offs that turn a prototype into a useful system.
researchIntro: Research on materials, energy, control, manufacturing, and reliable systems. Results keep their test conditions and scale attached: a material sample, laboratory device, and deployed system are different achievements.

title: Political Science and Institutions
tagline: How rules distribute power, organize disagreement, and make public decisions work.
description: Compare states, constitutions, voting rules, parties, public administration, courts, and international cooperation. Worked examples and research methods explain what institutions change, who they serve, and how to evaluate their results.
researchIntro: Research on institutions, public services, and collective decisions, selected for methods and lasting learning value. Every entry explains its question, method, and limitations. Campaign coverage, daily polling, opinion pieces, and party messaging are excluded.
